name: list
description:
List library scenes, objects, materials or robots, recipe add kinds, or these operations.
Example arguments: {"kind": "objects", "match": "peg"}

library.description: extra card library folders, searched first

name: scene
description:
Check a scene description without building it (fast); optionally save it as JSON or cards.
Example arguments: {"scene": {"objects": [{"add": "ground"}, {"add": "sphere", "name": "ball", "radius": 0.05, "pos": [0, 0, 0.3]}]}}

base.description: start from this library scene or file

liquid_accuracy.description: liquid particles 4 mm apart (default), 2 mm (super) or 1.5 mm (ultra)

keyword arguments of Scene.set_<set>, e.g. {"set": "heater", "name": "pan_floor", "temperature": 353.15} or {"set": "heat", "time_scale": 60}

name: vary
description:
Make n edited copies of one scene for visual and placement diversity, the same for the same seed: each free object (not robots, static, kinematic or held ones) moves within +-pos in x, y and +-yaw degrees, objects that touch move together, and a draw that overlaps or loses its support is redrawn; each look takes another texture of its family plus a small tint. Writes variant_000.json ... (pass one as scene to build, run or render) and variants.json (moves and textures); sheet adds contact_sheet.png.
Example arguments: {"scene": "demo_peg_d12", "n": 4, "pos": 0.01, "yaw": 10, "seed": 3, "out": "variants", "sheet": true}

name: compose
description:
Pick objects from the card library (Alloy's, alloy-assets, every imported library and your own folders), place them with support, clearance and clutter rules, run alloy.check after every placement and a full check at the end, and fix what the checks flag. Liquids and grains fill containers by volume or mass ('a mug with 200 ml of water'), pour as a stream, or pile at their angle of repose; cloth lies flat, drapes or hangs over the table edge; cables have a length, a gauge and ends plugged into objects. Returns every scene with its objects, soft items (amounts, routes, estimates), check report and metrics.
Example arguments: {"sentence": "a mug and two cubes on a table", "variations": 1, "out": "my_scenes"}

sentence.description: the scene in words, e.g. 'three nuts in a tray on a cluttered table'

spec.description: a SceneSpec as JSON instead of a sentence (alloy.compose.parse gives one)

variations.description: extra scenes with new poses and objects

check.description: full: load checks per placement + a full check; load; none

jitter.description: each world moves the free objects a little

worlds.description: parallel worlds in the saved scene cards

name: create
description:
Turn a mesh file, a photo or a text into an object card with a repaired watertight mesh, convex hulls, a visual GLB, and mass, friction and restitution with their sources (USER, CITED, LIBRARY or ESTIMATE with a range). Nothing is refused for a missing citation: estimates are labelled and listed under 'verify'. The card is drop-tested with alloy.check and written to `out` (use it with alloy.compose or Scene.add_object).
Example arguments: {"mesh": "part.stl", "units": "mm", "material": "steel", "out": "my_objects"}

mesh.description: mesh file: OBJ, STL, GLB/GLTF, PLY, or MJCF/URDF/USD

photo.description: a photo of the object (needs a 3D generator: $ALLOY_GEN3D_URL or a GPU)

text.description: a description, e.g. 'a red ceramic coffee mug' (needs a 3D generator)

name.description: card name, snake_case (default: from the file or text)

size.description: real longest side in metres (default: inferred, or the category's typical size)

mass.description: mass in kg (default: cited category values or an ESTIMATE)

mass_source.description: where the mass comes from (datasheet, scale reading)

material.description: library material name or a word: wood, steel, glass, plastic, ceramic...

category.description: what it is (mug, bowl, wrench...): improves the estimates

device.description: 'cpu' or 'cuda:0' for the drop test (default: the GPU if there is one)

name: audit
description:
Audit a scene the way a reviewer would, but automatically and with numbers: alloy.check over `rounds` seeds (each finding with the share of rounds it showed in and the command that replays it) and the bully agent over `episodes` random legal episodes (class, first tick, body, replay handle). Findings come sorted by severity, each with a suggested fix; ok is false when any finding is an error. A scene given as a recipe, Scene JSON, a .json file or a robot file is first written as cards to a folder that stays (`cards` in the reply), so the replays keep working after the call.
Example arguments: {"scene": "demo_peg_d12", "rounds": 2, "episodes": 8}

scene.description: scene: a library name, a .yaml path, Scene JSON or a recipe

episodes.description: bully agent episodes (random legal actuator commands or pushes)

worlds.description: worlds per check round (default 64 GPU / 2 CPU)

seconds.description: simulated seconds per check round and per bully episode (default: theirs)

device.description: 'cpu' or 'cuda:0' (default: the GPU if there is one)

library.description: extra card folders, searched first (e.g. the folder alloy create wrote to)

cards.description: folder to keep the scene's cards in when the scene is a recipe, Scene JSON, a .json file or a robot file (default: a folder per scene under ~/.cache/alloy/audit); the replays read it

name: fetch
description:
Files go to $ALLOY_CACHE/imports/<library>/ (default ~/.cache/alloy/imports/<library>/), where scenes, compose and the API find them; files already there with the right sha256 are not downloaded again. An object whose model uses another object's files (a composed cabinet's door panel and handle) brings that object too (`required`). Several fetches can fill one cache at the same time. The library is a public Hugging Face dataset: no login is needed (`hf auth login` or HF_TOKEN raises the Hub's rate limit).
Example arguments: {"library": "ycb_gso", "category": "ycb"}

library.description: a whole library: ycb_gso, robocasa, gymanything, objaverse, alloy

list.description: list libraries, categories and names instead of downloading

repo.description: dataset repo id (default $ALLOY_ASSETS_REPO, else Alloy's library)
